results.title: Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
Yes. ResStock’s **Geometry Wall Type data for Maine are known to be incorrect**, due to mislabeled county tax assessor data. For example, the issue report lists Maine’s single-family detached homes as approximately 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete—an implausible distribution confirmed by local researchers. The report says no fix has been implemented and that the team believes **all published ResStock datasets are affected**. [ResStock issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use nearby-state ResStock results, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For upgrade results where eligibility depends on wall type:** either reweight Maine’s results using nearby-state wall type distributions or use nearby-state results directly. Wood-frame-only insulation upgrades, for example, can apply to too few Maine homes because of this error. [Recommendations and impacts](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team does not currently believe energy consumption, emissions, or energy bills are significantly affected in baseline models or where upgrades are applied, but its investigation remains incomplete. [ResStock issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)
